items.title: Earl May interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2001
items.q: And he apparently sat in with Oscar when he first came up here and how he got his whole career started I think.

ctx.x: Right, exactly. It’s amazing how some people they sound. Look at Charlie Parker, the same thing. He would pick up your old horn that you were having—just like you say, and make it sound like wonderful.

Oscar is a name that is in one of my favorite stories because I’m a big Cannonball Adderley fan. And he apparently sat in with Oscar when he first came up here and how he got his whole career started I think.

Oscar was always helping somebody. He introduced me to Quincy Jones. Quincy was a little kid, he was about eighteen years old, as thin as that. He introduced me. And all these wonderful people that he would introduce me to, before they became famous. He was always trying to help somebody and bring them along. That’s what you’ve got to do.
